Cell outcomes reach ledgerd and commit once in effect. Desk fills become OutcomeRecords (DeskLedgerFeed) and qip-fastbrain's DeskShipper carries them to the P1 stream, acknowledging only after the fabric answers. The acknowledged watermark (DeskLedgerAcknowledged) is logged in the event log and resume_book re-queues unshipped fills. Loopback tests with the real ledger store show a resend after a crash, an outage or a fence posts once. No broker is deployed and no desk identity, grant or token exists (streams.local.json grants produce only to reflex:cell-local), so nothing ships in any environment.
gap: Deployment: a desk identity, grant and token, and a deployed broker. Only fastbrain ships; qip-api and the deep brain do not. Desk session is always 0; ids stay distinct across restarts only because resume_book continues the order counter past the log's (2026-10-17). The fill past the 10,000-record queue bound is booked, counted unledgered and not queued; the next acknowledgement that makes room re-derives it from the event log and queues it in chain order (tested with 10,001 real fills, and equal to what a restart re-queues). Delivery is slow, about 3.8 seconds a batch of ~127 records (10,000 records took ~300s): the quota is not the limit (a thousand records saw no quota refusal); the time is consistent with the producer's Archived-ack metadata polls, which sleep 50ms, 200ms, 800ms, 3.2s between polls. Not measured further. A quota refusal is now waited out for the broker's named time instead of the shipper's ladder. Tests are example-based, not a property test over redelivery and crash schedules. No fastbrain binary -> real broker -> ledgerd run.
notes: Dedup is by (cell, session, seq, digest) chain continuity, not a bare event id; equivalent or stronger.
